clue.text: Leaf chewed by Persian shah to gain universal knowledge?

parts.note: paan or pan is the betel leaf chewed across South Asia, often with areca nut
Sophy is an old English title for the shah of Persia, from the Safavid dynasty

explanation.surface: A Persian ruler chews a leaf in the hope of becoming all-knowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaf chewed' is not an anagram signal: paan is the betel leaf chewed in South Asia, and Sophy is what Elizabethan writers called the Persian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Pansophy is the claim to complete wisdom covering every branch of learning, i.e. universal knowledge.

clue.text: A little tart?

parts.note: looks like a small pastry, but reads as an adjective: slightly sour in taste

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' tempts you towards pastries; here it is the adjective sharp, and 'a little' tones it down to mildly sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidulous describes something somewhat acid or sour, so only a little tart rather than very sharp.

clue.text: As a means of defence, animal assaults the nose

definitions.text: As a means of defence, animal assaults the nose

parts.words: As a means of defence, animal assaults the nose
parts.note: describes a black-and-white mammal that protects itself by spraying a foul-smelling liquid at attackers

explanation.surface: A creature defends itself by attacking an enemy's sense of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped mammal fends off predators with a pungent musky spray, an assault on the nose.

clue.text: Start modelling a ripe peach using this substance

indicators.note: the letters are used up and reworked, pointing to a rearrangement of the pool
the start of the word modelling is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written, letters for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin sculpting a ripe peach out of some craft material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' picks M from 'modelling'; that M joins the letters of A RIPE PEACH and 'using' signals the rearrangement of all eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Papier-mache is a moulding material of pulped paper and paste, a substance used for modelling.

clue.text: Farm worker with three feet, on British isle

parts.note: a yard is a measure equal to three feet
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A labourer on a farm with three feet lives on a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardman is a labourer who works in a farmyard or stockyard.

clue.text: With Puerto Rico, alliance between a number of states is accepted custom

parts.words: alliance between a number of states
parts.note: the Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan

explanation.surface: Puerto Rico joining a coalition of nations becomes established practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Praxis means established practice, the customary way something is done as opposed to theory.

clue.text: Favouring the expert

definitions.meaning: being for something, as in arguments for and against

explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means in support of; as a noun it is short for professional, a skilled practitioner.

clue.text: A section intended, say, to be flat

parts.note: a part is a section of something

indicators.note: say tells us the word for intended is spoken, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: meant is the past of mean, to intend

explanation.surface: A portion of something was designed to be level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns MEANT into its sound-alike ending MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartment is the American and formal word for a flat, a set of rooms for living in.

clue.text: One does little to get butcher riled

indicators.note: to butcher something is to mangle it, so the word riled is hacked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lazy annoys the butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher' looks like a tradesman but is a verb telling you to mangle RILED.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person, someone who does very little work.

clue.text: The substitute is in it

parts.note: a stand-in serves in place of another, i.e. completes the phrase 'in ___ of'

explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place or stead, so whatever substitutes for another is said to be in its stead.

clue.text: Fellow in moral tale may be venial

indicators.note: in places the fellow within the story

parts.note: a parable is a short story teaching a moral lesson
a don is a fellow or tutor at a university college

explanation.surface: A college fellow appearing in a fable may be only a minor sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A venial sin or fault is slight enough to be forgiven, hence excusable.

clue.text: Fastening that might cave in under pressure?

definitions.meaning: a clasp on a belt or strap
to give way or crumple when force is applied

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a clasp for a belt; as a verb it means to collapse or bend under strain.

clue.text: Cap for women rests uneasily on crooks

parts.note: a mob cap is a large frilled cap worn indoors by women in the 18th and 19th centuries

indicators.note: the word rests sits uncomfortably, its letters shifted out of order

explanation.surface: A woman's bonnet lies awkwardly on a pair of villains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasily' signals a rearrangement of the word rests. A mob cap is a frilled indoor bonnet of the Georgian era, so 'Cap' is not a lid or a limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobsters are gangsters, members of organised criminal gangs.

clue.text: Landmine creating a confusion of rock and stubble

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder to make something new

explanation.surface: An explosive leaves stones and stubble jumbled up.
explanation.walkthrough: The joined letters of ROCK and STUBBLE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Blockbuster was the wartime name for a huge bomb able to destroy a whole block, applied loosely to a big mine.

clue.text: Left aboard with a group of chaps to add notes when gliding

parts.note: on board ship the left-hand side is port
men are a group of chaps
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man on deck joins some fellows to add music played with a slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'add' is a link: the pieces are simply lined up.
explanation.definitionFit: Portamento is a smooth slide in pitch from one musical note to the next.

clue.text: What's-his-name is skinny and toothless

parts.note: thin means skinny
someone gummy shows gums with no teeth

explanation.surface: A person whose name you forget is lean and has lost their teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Thingummy is a placeholder used for a person or thing whose name you cannot recall.

clue.text: One test out of a million

parts.note: ex means out of or former

explanation.surface: Only one assessment in a million is worth sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge, so one exam is a single test.

clue.text: Material to fashion altar base

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape something, so the letters of altar base are moulded anew

explanation.surface: Stone used to craft the foot of an altar.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine translucent stone, a material used for carving.

clue.text: Drink from a plastic bottle

indicators.note: from tells us the drink is taken out of the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Have a swig straight out of a plastic bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' holds the wine inside it; 'a' and 'bottle' just fill out the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so a drink.

clue.text: Two winged creatures in this willow

parts.note: a cricket is a winged chirping insect
a bat is a flying mammal with wings

explanation.surface: A pair of flying animals perch in a willow tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willow' looks like the tree but stands for what is carved from it; cricket is the British bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats for the sport of cricket are traditionally made of willow, so the wood names the bat.

clue.text: Settle everyone after this month

indicators.note: after places everyone below the month in this down entry

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is old business-letter shorthand for the current month
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Get everyone sorted once this month is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is to settle them in a place or position.

clue.text: Sets off with the first guys who know the ropes

indicators.note: the first letter of the word the is taken

parts.note: riggers handle the ropes and rigging on a ship or stage

explanation.surface: Things begin when the leading crew members, experienced sailors, arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Triggers means sets in motion, as when an event sets off a reaction.

clue.text: Gunmen holding note up to a girl

indicators.note: holding means the gunners enclose the reversed note

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the note is read from bottom to top

parts.note: doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Armed men keep a message to deliver to a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DOH into HOD, which RA holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a girl's given name, from the Greek for rose.

clue.text: Heartening to have a meal at new pub

indicators.note: new means the word pub is made over in a fresh order

parts.note: eat means to have a meal

explanation.surface: Dining at a newly opened pub is an encouraging experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means cheerful and optimistic, the mood of something encouraging.

clue.text: Runner takes nothing with junket

parts.note: a runner bean is a climbing bean grown in British gardens
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An athlete comes away empty-handed from a free trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it is the runner bean.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a celebration or outing, much like a junket or jolly.

clue.text: Order social worker to be the one who takes charge

parts.note: to command is to order
an ant is a social insect, and many are worker ants

explanation.surface: Telling a social worker to lead the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a council employee but an insect living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A commandant is the officer in charge of a military establishment.

clue.text: This is not French, whichever way you view it

indicators.note: the word reads the same from either end, top to bottom or bottom to top

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark that something is foreign to French, viewed from any angle.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the word for no or not is non.

clue.text: Stake taken from elephant enclosure

indicators.note: the stake is extracted from the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A post removed from the enclosure for elephants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' looks like a fence post for the enclosure, but it is a gambling bet.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put into the pot before cards are dealt in poker.

clue.text: Refuse to allow unlimited number to enter the plant

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to ban is to refuse to allow
any number means no limit on the count

explanation.surface: A ban on letting an endless crowd into the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a works, but it is the Indian fig tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The banyan is an Indian fig tree whose aerial roots grow into new trunks.

clue.text: Old port to which sailors may be directed

definitions.meaning: the former name for the left-hand side of a ship

definitions.text: to which sailors may be directed
definitions.meaning: a side of the vessel that crew can be ordered towards

explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the archaic term for the left side of a ship, later replaced by port, and a direction sailors were sent.
